**Amazon Q Developer** is not supported yet. This is a self-contained first contribution: the scaffold
writes the code, the fixtures and the registration, and what is left is the part below.

Read [`docs/writing-an-adapter.md`](../../docs/writing-an-adapter.md) first — it is the
whole workflow, and it is written for someone who has never seen this codebase.

## What Amazon Q Developer reads

- `.amazonq/rules/` at the project root: "Project rules are defined in Markdown files in the
  project's `{project-root}/.amazonq/rules` folder." Subdirectories are supported, e.g.
  `.amazonq/rules/frontend/react.rule.md`.

Rules are picked up automatically for the project; the CLI can also add them to a session
with `/context add`.

**Documentation:** Amazon Q Developer — Creating project rules — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/en_us/amazonq/latest/qdeveloper-ug/third-party-context-project-rules.html
_(read 2026-09-04; re-read it before you file the precedence data, and put the date you
actually read it in `retrieved`.)_

## What to build

- **Adapter id:** `amazon-q`
- **Artifact to generate:** `.amazonq/rules/<slug>.md`, one file per rule
- **Rendering:** one plain Markdown file per rule, no frontmatter
- **Resolution:** `additive` — every rule file in the folder is used as context

## The part that needs care

There is no frontmatter here at all, so a glob-scoped rule has to state its scope in prose —
`renderConcatenated({ showGlobs: true })` does that, and the behaviour is documented as
lossy rather than silent.

Check the CLI documentation as well as the page above before writing `docs.ts`. Amazon Q
ships in several surfaces (CLI, IDE plugins, GitLab/GitHub) and they do not all read the
same paths. Encode only what you can cite.

## Steps

```bash
rulegate adapter new amazon-q          # prints the plan
rulegate adapter new amazon-q --yes    # applies it
pnpm install && pnpm test           # green as generated
```

1. Hand-write `fixtures/amazon-q/expected/` from the documentation above, **before** touching
   `write()`. A golden generated by the adapter it checks proves only that the adapter
   agrees with itself.
2. Implement `detect` → `read` → `write` until the golden passes byte-exact.
3. Fill in `packages/adapters/amazon-q/src/docs.ts` — every placeholder there is `TODO`, and
   dated `1970-01-01` so an unverified claim cannot be mistaken for a verified one.
4. Run Amazon Q Developer against the generated config and confirm it actually loads. Say so in the PR,
   with the version you tested.
5. Add `amazon-q` to `.rulegate/rulegate.yaml` and run `rulegate sync` — this repository
   dogfoods every adapter it ships. Commit the generated file with your change.

## Done when

- `pnpm verify` is clean and `fixtures/amazon-q/expected/` was written by hand, from the docs
- `detect` fixtures: `positive/` detected, `negative/` not
- `src/docs.ts` carries a real source URL, a real `retrieved` date, and the Amazon Q Developer version
  you verified against
- You ran the real tool and it loaded the file

Ask anything in the comments — an unanswerable question here is a bug in this issue.
